newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai stocks end down at noon despite HK return.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai stocks end down at noon despite HK return.

text.p: Shanghai stocks closed sharply lower on Wednesday morning with investors ignoring the euphoria over the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule on Monday, brokers said.
The foreign currency B share index fell 1.227 points or 1.51 percent to end the morning session at 80.251 points on volume of 3.426 million shares worth $1.935 million.
The domestic currency A share index plunged 43.951 points or 3.36 percent to 1,262.827 points on volume of 158.660 million shares worth 2.421 billion yuan in morning trading.
"The handover euphoria has faded and the market is lacking support," said one broker. "The technical charts indicate a downward trend and it is hard to judge where the indices will find support."

Despite China's nationwide happiness over the return of the British colony of Hong Kong, investors had already digested the news and are now looking for fresh clues on the direction of the market, brokers said.
"The B shares were hurt by falls in A shares," said another broker. "But volume was relatively thin, indicating uncertainty over the market's direction after the handover."

Investors would likely look towards the announcement of positive 1997 interim results in July and August and possible moves by the government to loosen credit in the second half of 1997 before buying decisively, brokers said.
"Investors are now looking at interim results," said an analyst at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai. "Credit easing or some other sort of stimulus could also provide direction."
Interim results of Shanghai-listed A and B share firms are generally expected to be better than for the first half of 1996, but any buying would be selective, brokers said.
Of 45 B shares, 35 traded with 19 down, nine up and seven flat.
Shanghai Sanmao Textile Co was the sharpest B share loser, plunging $0.016 or 9.88 percent to $0.146 on poor interim results prospects.

The B index will likely find support at around 80 points in afternoon trading on some institutional buying, but most investors are unwilling to enter the market due to rumours that negative news will soon emerge, brokers said.
